source.title: WRC Digest 2024-Q1
source.content:
Dear WCA Community,

So far, this year has been a productive one for the WRC! We would like to share some of our progress with you.

Firstly, 10 new members joined the WRC ([committee page](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/teams-committees-councils#wrc)) and their contributions have been extremely helpful to the team. We’re looking forward to seeing what the future holds for the WRC and how this shapes our decisions and responses to the community.

For added clarity, we have released two different visual guides, one for [5b5f](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#5b5f) and one for [3j](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#3j). We aim to issue more guidance to the WCA community for other regulations as we see fit.

With more cubers than ever, the WCA has been able to organize a huge number of competitions! Naturally, the increase in competitions comes with an increase in incidents. Here are some of the more notable resolved incidents:

1. A solving station with a QiYi timer was set up near the competing area, in order for competitors to familiarize themselves with how to handle timers so as to not damage the official Speed Stacks timers at the solving stations. Unfortunately, many competitors and staff confused this “training station” for an official station, and this non-permitted timer was used for several attempts, violating [Regulation 7f1a](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#7f1a). Because it was impossible to determine with certainty which attempts used the timer, the WRC decided to remove all results for this competition.
2. A competitor attempted to stop the timer without their palms facing down, violating [A4b](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#A4b). Immediately after this, they attempted to stop the timer again with their palms correctly facing down. Both competitor and judge were unsure when the timer was actually stopped, and no video evidence was available. Since no extra attempt was available the WRC has decided to keep the original time as it is not clear if the competitor has done anything wrong.
3. A competitor had their hands quite close to a covered clock pre-inspection and, as the judge lifted the cover, the clock fell over and a turn was unintentionally applied by the competitor to one of the dials. While the puzzle falling over was the judge's fault, the move was applied by the competitor, which led to a change in the inner clock faces that counts as a DNF ([F4](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#F4)). Also, since any moves applied by the competitor in inspection (except those that are within the limits outlined by [10f](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#10f)) are illegal ([A3c1](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#A3c1)), the WRC decided that the correct penalty was a DNF.
4. After stopping the timer the competitor turned a Pyraminx tip that was misaligned by 120 degrees, but there was disagreement between the judge and the competitor whether it was turned more than 60 degrees or less. While turns greater than 60 degrees count as a move ([10f3](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#10f3)), and applying a move after stopping the timer is a DNF ([A6e1](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#A6e1)), merely touching the puzzle without applying a move is a +2 ([A6e2](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#A6e2)). The WRC decided that the correct penalty is DNF since it is possible that a move has been applied.
5. In an unconventional situation, a power cut that ensued during an FMC attempt resulted in poor lighting for about 3 minutes, during which the attempt was “paused” and the lost time added to the end of the attempt for all competitors. After an internal voting process, the WRC decided that the decision of the delegates to have everyone stop for 3 minutes didn’t pose an unfair advantage to any competitor in any way. In general, the WRC advised against giving extra time for an FMC attempt, and to instead cancel the attempt altogether or give an extra attempt if at all possible.
6. A judge applied an unintentional turn to a clock as they were checking to see if it was solved after a competitor’s attempt was done. This created a difficulty in verifying that the competitor had actually solved the puzzle by the end of their attempt. However, upon reviewing video evidence, the WRC was able to conclude that the exact state of the back of the clock was only possible with the one move made by the judge and that it would have been solved otherwise. On these grounds, the puzzle was considered solved by the competitor.
8. Several competitions utilizing TimeBase reported incidents where the signed results on the score sheets differed from the results logged on TimeBase databases. As TimeBase is an unofficial system not yet defined in the Regulations, a discussion between the WRC and WRT and a subsequent ruling by the WCA Board came to the conclusion that the score sheet results should stand. Due to the fact that score sheets are defined as the source material for results, it should be the main source that should be deferred to in case of such a discrepancy. While systems similar to TimeBase have the potential to dramatically improve the flow of competitions and to greatly simplify the work needed to ensure that competitions run smoothly, it is not yet officially endorsed, and as such disputes concerning errors in results concerning them will continue to use scorecards as reference.
9. A competitor handed in an FMC solution containing an arrow. The solution would have been correct without the arrow, and even with the arrow the move sequence was still unambiguous ([E2c2](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#E2c2)). However, since the arrow was written in a place where it had to be counted as part of the solution, and since [E2c4+](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/guidelines.html#E2c4+) explicitly mentions arrows as forbidden symbols, the delegates decided to DNF the attempt. The WRC and the Board decided to uphold this decision following two appeals, but the WRC will revisit this part of the FMC regulations in the next regulation cycle.
10. A competitor forgot to lift a sight blocker attached to a harmonica holder during the execution phase of their solve. The competitor had started execution for around 30 seconds before the Delegate noticed the situation and a sight blocker was placed. Seeing that it is the judge’s responsibility to ensure that there is an opaque sight blocker as per [Regulation B4c](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#B4c), in addition to the fact that the competitor was established as trustworthy and did not appear to have taken advantage of the situation, the original result was allowed to stand under [Guideline B4c++](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/guidelines.html#B4c++).
11. Post-competition, a competitor found that two attempts of their average had been incorrectly scrambled by the same scrambler using a different orientation than the standard green-front, white-top. Events potentially affected by a z2 scrambling error (including 3x3) are not usually orientation dependent, because most of these events have their vast majority of competitors as dual-color neutral. The WRC found that since most competitors are able to start their attempts on opposite colors, the attempt would be allowed to stand seeing as there was no significant advantage or disadvantage posed to the competitor. 

If you have any questions for the WRC, feel free to reach out to us via [email](regulations@worldcubeassociation.org) or on the [WCA Forum](https://forum.worldcubeassociation.org/c/regulations/5)!

translation.title: WCA 规则委员会工作简报：2024 年第一季度
translation.content:
亲爱的 WCA 社区成员：

今年以来，WCA 规则委员会（WRC）的工作进展顺利，我们想和大家分享一些近况。

首先，WRC 迎来了 10 名新成员（见[委员会页面](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/teams-committees-councils#wrc)）。他们为团队提供了很大的帮助。我们期待他们带来的新变化，也期待这些变化如何影响委员会的决策以及与社区的沟通。

为了让规则更容易理解，我们发布了两份图解，分别说明 [5b5f](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#5b5f) 和 [3j](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#3j)。今后，我们也会根据需要，为其他规则提供更多说明。

随着魔友人数不断增加，WCA 举办的比赛数量也大幅增长。比赛多了，意外情况也随之增多。以下是部分已处理的典型事件：

1. 某场比赛在比赛区域附近设置了一个使用奇艺计时器的练习台，供选手熟悉计时器操作，避免损坏正式比赛台上的 Speed Stacks 计时器。然而，不少选手和工作人员误将其当作正式比赛台，导致多次还原使用了不允许使用的计时器，违反了[规则 7f1a](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#7f1a)。由于无法确定哪些还原使用了该计时器，WRC 决定删除这场比赛的全部成绩。
2. 一名选手第一次尝试停表时手掌没有朝下，违反了 [A4b](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#A4b)。随后，他立即将手掌正确朝下，再次尝试停表。选手和裁判都不确定计时器究竟在哪一次接触时停止，也没有视频证据。由于无法安排额外还原，而且不能确定选手是否确有违规，WRC 决定保留原成绩。
3. 观察开始前，一名选手的双手离盖住的魔表较近。裁判掀开遮盖物时，魔表倒下，选手无意中转动了其中一个转轮。虽然魔表倒下是裁判造成的，但转动是由选手施加的，且改变了内部指针的位置，应判为 DNF（[F4](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#F4)）。此外，观察期间选手进行的任何转动，除在 [10f](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#10f) 所规定限度内的转动外，均属违规（[A3c1](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#A3c1)）。因此，WRC 认定应判为 DNF。
4. 一名选手停表后转动了一个偏离 120 度的金字塔角尖，但裁判和选手对实际转动是否超过 60 度存在分歧。超过 60 度的转动算作一步（[10f3](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#10f3)），停表后转动一步应判 DNF（[A6e1](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#A6e1)）；仅触碰魔方而没有转动则罚时 2 秒（[A6e2](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#A6e2)）。由于存在选手已经转动一步的可能，WRC 决定判为 DNF。
5. 一次较为特殊的最少步还原中，停电造成约 3 分钟的照明不足。比赛因此“暂停”，并在结束时为所有选手补回这段时间。经内部投票，WRC 认为，代表让所有选手共同停下 3 分钟的做法没有给任何选手带来不公平的优势。不过，通常情况下，WRC 不建议为最少步还原延时；应直接取消该次还原，或在条件允许时安排额外还原。
6. 一名选手完成魔表还原后，裁判在检查是否还原时无意中转动了一步，导致难以确认停表时是否已经还原。WRC 查看视频后认定，魔表背面当时的具体状态只能由裁判的那一步转动造成；如果没有这一步，魔表应处于还原状态。因此，该次还原被认定为成功。
8. 多场使用 TimeBase 的比赛报告，成绩单上经签名确认的成绩与 TimeBase 数据库记录不一致。TimeBase 尚未在规则中定义，属于非官方系统。经 WRC 与 WCA 成绩组（WRT）讨论，并由 WCA 董事会裁定，应以成绩单上的成绩为准。规则将成绩单定义为成绩的原始材料，因此发生此类不一致时，应优先依据成绩单。TimeBase 及类似系统有望大幅改善比赛流程、减轻赛事运行的工作量，但目前尚未获官方认可，涉及这类系统成绩错误的争议仍将以成绩单为依据。
9. 一名选手提交的最少步解法中带有一个箭头。不含箭头时，解法是正确的；即使保留箭头，转动顺序也没有歧义（[E2c2](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#E2c2)）。但箭头所在的位置必须视为解法的一部分，而 [E2c4+](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/guidelines.html#E2c4+) 明确将箭头列为禁用符号，因此代表判该次还原为 DNF。经过两次申诉，WRC 和董事会决定维持原判。不过，WRC 会在下一轮规则修订中重新讨论最少步规则的这一部分。
10. 一名选手进入盲拧还原阶段时，忘记抬起固定在口琴架上的遮挡板。约 30 秒后，代表发现问题并放置了遮挡板。根据[规则 B4c](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/#B4c)，确保使用不透明遮挡板是裁判的责任；同时，该选手被认定为可信，也没有表现出利用这一情况的迹象。因此，根据[指南 B4c++](https://www.worldcubeassociation.org/regulations/guidelines.html#B4c++)，原成绩得以保留。
11. 赛后，一名选手发现，自己一组平均中的两次还原由同一名打乱员按非标准的朝向打乱，而标准朝向应为绿前白上。可能受 z2 打乱朝向错误影响的项目（包括三阶）通常不依赖特定朝向，因为这些项目中的绝大多数选手都能使用两个相对颜色作为起始面。WRC 认为，由于多数选手可以从相对的两个颜色开始还原，该错误没有给选手带来明显优势或劣势，因此允许保留成绩。

如有问题，欢迎通过[邮件](regulations@worldcubeassociation.org)或 [WCA 论坛](https://forum.worldcubeassociation.org/c/regulations/5)联系 WRC！
notes: 原文列表从 6 跳至 8，保留原编号。原文第 2 项关于停表引用 A4b，按原文保留，未擅改规则编号。原文第 11 项对双底选手比例的判断按历史公告译出。

notes: 全文已审：10项案例编号原文跳过7，中文保留；第2项原文为停表却引用A4b（启动计时器规则），属于源文规则引用疑点，不擅自替换。数字、处罚、不确定性及其余情节译义一致。
